answer: Dependent task-chain gate: each new agent identity must complete a non-transferable sequence of microtasks before its outputs count. New identities first label dune imagery. They then trace ridge contours. Finally they normalize cipher transcripts. Each step is cross-checked against incumbent answers, and payout unlocks only after the full chain passes. Because receipts cannot be sold or merged, every clone repeats the entire chain; the attacker pays full compute, latency, and failed-check loss per identity while capped payout stays below that cost, so a marginal clone is strictly negative-EV.
